title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is currently balancing on the fine line between innovation and operational challenges. With funding flowing into rocket technologies and satellite capabilities, the focus remains on addressing the underlying infrastructure issues that could derail progress.

themes.title: Funding Fuels Rocket Ambitions
themes.body: Venus Aerospace's recent $91 million raise highlights a growing interest in advanced propulsion technologies. Investors are clearly betting that the next generation of rockets will be the key to unlocking new markets.

themes.title: Spaceports in Distress
themes.body: The government's struggle to address strained spaceports is becoming increasingly apparent, as launch schedules clash with limited infrastructure. This could hinder the ambitious plans of both commercial and military players in the coming years.

themes.title: Defense Tech IPOs on the Horizon
themes.body: The defense-tech sector is showing signs of life as the IPO window begins to crack open, presenting opportunities for startups eager to capitalize on government contracts. This could lead to a reshuffling of the competitive landscape as new players enter the fray.

themes.title: Space Force Expands Partnerships
themes.body: The Space Force's addition of Relativity and Impulse Space to its national security launch program signals a strategic shift towards leveraging commercial capabilities. This partnership could enhance the U.S.'s launch resilience amid growing global competition.
